What is Ignosticism/Igtheism?

Ignosticism/Igtheism is the idea that coherent and falsifiable definitions of all religious terms (including God) must be must be given before any meaningful discussion can take place about them. In absence of such a definition (which happens often in online discourse), the Ignostic/Igtheist position becomes same as theological noncognitivism.

For example, (unlike theists, atheists or agnostics) for an Igtheist the statement "God exists" doesn't have meaning or truth value on its own. This statement gets meaning and truth value only after the term "God" is defined.

Philosopher Theodore Drange illustrates further:

"An atheist would say, 'I don't believe God exists';

an agnostic would say, 'I don't know whether or not God exists';

and an ignostic would say, 'I don't know what you mean when you say, "God exists" .

Why this subverse?

This subverse is for theists, atheists and agnostics to put expound their own definitions of basic theological entities (such as God) and to build their theologies from the basics. Expect feedback, suggestions and criticism from other members. A basic knowledge and application of logic is desirable.
